applies_to: Trane VAV terminal units with the Symbio 210 programmable controller running the factory VAV programs (space temperature, ventilation flow and flow tracking control).
summary: The Symbio 210 is Trane's programmable VAV box controller. With the factory VAV program it exposes about 120 objects with short instances (AI 1, AV 14, MV 6...). The BAS sends setpoints, sensor values and occupancy through the '... BAS' and '... Request' objects; the BAS value objects ship Out of Service and must be put In Service before the controller uses them. Which objects exist depends on the application (STC, VFC or FTC) and the heat and fan options.
notes: The guide has no read/write column. Access is inferred: inputs, hardware outputs and Active/Status/Diagnostic/auto-commissioning results are read-only; the BAS, Request, Override, setpoint and configuration value objects are writable.

Point availability depends on the application (Space Temperature Control, Ventilation Flow Control, Flow Tracking Control) and the heat type; the guide's Table 9 marks which applications use each point.
Units follow the controller's system units (IP or SI). AV 2 and AV 8 are printed with pressure units although they hold airflow values; they are kept as printed.
The PDF at this URL prints document number BAS-SVP043A-EN, June 2021, on its pages.
Alarm objects: AI 1, AI 2, AI 4 and AI 5 go to fault when the sensor fails, and the Diagnostic BVs (BV 3, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13) carry notification classes 2-4.

source.title: Integration Guide: Symbio 210 Programmable Controller for Variable-Air-Volume (VAV) Boxes

integration.summary: Write occupancy to MV 6 Occupancy Request and the space setpoint to AV 27 Space Temperature Setpoint BAS after putting it In Service. Read AV 59 Space Temperature Active, AV 20 Discharge Air Flow and AV 13 Air Flow Setpoint Active. If the BMS supplies space temperature or CO2, put AV 14/AV 22 In Service and rewrite them every 15 minutes.

minimum_points.name: Heat Cool Mode Request
minimum_points.why: Heat/cool mode command from the BMS

minimum_points.name: Space Temperature Setpoint BAS
minimum_points.why: Space setpoint; put In Service before writing

integration.enable: No enable point. The '... BAS' value objects ship Out of Service and are ignored until the BMS (or Tracer SC) puts them In Service. Symbio UI (Tools > BAS Control Selection) chooses BAS or Local as the source for each sensor and setpoint.
integration.heartbeat: AV 14 Space Temperature BAS and AV 22 Space CO2 Concentration BAS must be written at least every 15 minutes while In Service; otherwise the controller puts the point in fault.
integration.remote_sensors: Space temperature goes to AV 14, CO2 to AV 22 and supply air temperature to AV 29, each after putting the object In Service. AV 59, AV 50 and AV 60 show the values in use. Select BAS as the source in Symbio UI BAS Control Selection.
setup: Three rotary switches set a three-digit address used as both the MS/TP MAC address and the Device ID; valid MAC addresses are 001-127.
Symbio UI is a web page served over the USB service port at http://198.80.18.1; it sets protocol, IP settings, name, time and system units.
Changing system units (IP/SI) or protocol settings restarts the controller.
gotchas: Writes to BAS objects do nothing while they are Out of Service (the factory default).
MV 2 Air Flow Override and MV 3 Water Valve Override force the box; release them when done.
AV 37 Space Temp Setpoint Default and the airflow min/max setpoints are commissioning values, not for cyclic writes.
